what_it_does:
An all-in-one DLSS tool for Windows and NVIDIA RTX. In this tool, "DLSS 5" means DLSS 5 Neural Rendering (NR). This is NVIDIA's AI post-process that re-lights the finished frame (materials, skin, lighting). Its runtime is a separate NGX snippet, nvngx_dlssnr.dll (310.8.x, or 310.9.16 since 2026-10-16). It is NOT a newer SR preset or transformer model K/L/M, and NOT a newer nvngx_dlss.dll. NR has two models. Preset A (value 1) is the September CC_Control_..._2026_07_04 model. Preset B (value 2) is the October hnet-crazy-cuckoo-small-fp8 model: about 24% smaller, ~20% less VRAM and faster (author measured 5.9 ms vs 3.4 ms in Witcher 3). Value 0 or unset falls back to B in 310.9.16. Games do not call NR themselves, so the tool injects a "consumer" that drives the NR runtime: a ReShade add-on (RenoDX DLSS5 by lecram, ShortFuse's RenoDX DLSS Tool multipass, DLSS5-Feeder, GITC Uplift) or an OptiScaler DLSS-NR fork. It also:
- updates SR, RR and FG DLLs (nvngx_dlss/dlssd/dlssg) to newer NVIDIA versions
- sets per-game NVIDIA driver profile (DRS) DLSS overrides: SR preset K/L/M/J/F/E/D and mode DLAA..Ultra Performance, RR preset D/E/F, FG preset A/B/C and fixed 2x-6x or dynamic multi frame generation
- toggles the NGX DLSS indicator
- installs RenoDX HDR mods
- backs up everything and restores with one click
mechanism:
Read from source in app/src/core/apply.js, nr-model.js, nv-drs.js, compatibility.js, install-guards.js, components.js and tools/NvDrs.cs.

1. Components download (components.js, component-pins.js). Downloads go to %APPDATA%\dlss5-swapper\payload. Each archive is SHA-256-pinned, and NVIDIA files must pass an Authenticode check (WinVerifyTrust, signer "NVIDIA Corporation", product "NVIDIA DLSSNR", version >= 310.8).
- The DLSS 5 runtime is NVIDIA_NR, version 310.9.16.0, from https://github.com/RankFTW/rhi-repo/releases/download/dlssnr-310.9.16-nvidia/nvngx_dlssnr_310.9.16-nvidia.zip. Archive sha256 5277355f...e09f6, DLL sha256 2bc19bc0...e28789f. It is an unmodified NVIDIA-signed DLL taken from games (NBA 2K27, Hogwarts Legacy). It is NOT in the official NVIDIA/DLSS SDK repo. Users may import their own DLL instead.
- An optional "LEGACY_NR" 310.8.SF-v2 build for RTX 20/30/40 comes from rhi-repo (dlssnr-310.8.SF-v2): archive 1da35941..., DLL 6eb209e7..., about 166 MB. It is community-modified, not NVIDIA-signed, supports model A only and runs at roughly half the fps. It is only downloaded after a warning.
- SR/RR/FG DLLs come from the GitHub releases API for NVIDIA/DLSS and from raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/DLSS/<tag>/lib/Windows_x86_64/rel/<file>.
- Streamline 2.13 sl.*.dll and the RenoDX add-ons (lecram 8.5.0-rc10, ShortFuse DLSS Tool SF 26.1025) come from rhi-repo.
- ReShade 6.8.0 Addon setup comes from reshade.me. DLL and json are read out of the zip inside the setup, so it is not executed except as the official setup.
- DLSS5-Feeder 2.0.0 comes from jlrouzies-fr/DLSS5-Feeder.
- OptiScaler DLSS-NR builds come from Dagherbou/OptiScaler_DLSSNR and jlrouzies-fr/OptiScaler-DLSSNR-PreSR-Multipass.
- GITC Uplift 2.0.0, dgVoodoo 2.87.6 and LumeniteFX also come from their own repos.

2. Choosing a route per game (shared/install-routes.js). scan.js detects the exe, bitness, graphics API (dxgi/d3d9/opengl/vulkan) and any DLSS or Streamline DLLs.
- 'native': lecram RenoDX + ReShade. DX12, 64-bit, the game ships its own nvngx_dlss.dll. This is the recommended route.
- 'renodx': ShortFuse multipass. DX11/DX12 64-bit and D3D9 64-bit.
- 'combo': lecram + ShortFuse with ForeignNr=observe. Experimental.
- 'feeder': DLSS5-Feeder for games without DLSS, including DX9-12, Vulkan, OpenGL, 32-bit and emulators. DX8/DDraw goes through dgVoodoo.
- 'uplift' and 'lecram12' (a paid lecram build the user imports).
- 'optiscaler': 64-bit dxgi/vulkan games with native DLSS.
- On AMD/Intel only 'optiscaler' is offered, using janblade's vendor-neutral DirectML port.

3. Install, 'native' route (applySwap in apply.js):
- Refuses if the exe folder is not writable or the NR payload is missing.
- Starts a backup manifest in <gameDir>\_DLSS5_Backup\manifest.json. It records added files, replaced files (with old/new version), added dirs and ReShade state.
- Upgrades every nvngx_dlss/dlssd/dlssg/dlssnr.dll the game already has, including nested Unreal ThirdParty paths. Same bitness only. It never downgrades and skips files that are already the same version. sl.* files are never touched.
- Always copies nvngx_dlssnr.dll next to the game exe, and nvngx_dlss.dll only if it is missing and requested.
- For multipass, copies Streamline sl.*.dll only if the game has no sl.interposer.dll of its own.
- Copies the consumer add-on next to the exe: renodx-dlss5.addon64, ShortFuse's tool, or dlss5-nr.addon64 for lecram v11/v12. Rival consumers are moved aside. Their own AiO SF Toggle add-on adds an F6 on/off key.
- Installs add-on ReShade under the right proxy name (dxgi.dll, d3d9.dll, opengl32.dll, or a global Vulkan layer registration) and writes ReShade.ini.
- Refuses on loader conflicts: multiple ReShade hooks, ASI ReShade, foreign proxies. It also refuses for Mod Organizer "Stock Game" folders. An old D3DCompiler_47.dll (<10.x) beside the exe is retired, because NR is compiled as cs_5_1.

4. Choosing the NR model (nr-model.js). The NR runtime ignores the driver profile; the preset is passed by the consumer. The tool walks the game folder (depth 6) and writes an INI value:
- ReShade.ini [RenoDX.DLSS5] NRPreset=1|2, or
- OptiScaler.ini [DlssNr] Preset=1|2. This becomes the NGX parameter DLSSNR.Hint.Render.Preset.

5. NVIDIA DRS profile (nv-drs.js plus nv-drs.exe built from tools/NvDrs.cs with the C# compiler that ships with Windows).
- It P/Invokes nvapi64.dll nvapi_QueryInterface: Initialize, DRS_CreateSession, LoadSettings, FindApplicationByName, then CreateProfile "DLSS5 Swapper - <exe>" + CreateApplication if missing, then SetSetting/DeleteProfileSetting and SaveSettings.
- Allowed setting IDs:
  - SR: 0x10E41E01 latest on/off; 0x10E41DF3 preset (0xFFFFFF recommended, 0xD=M, 0xC=L, 0xB=K, 0xA=J, 6/5/4=F/E/D); 0x10AFB768 force mode (4 DLAA, 2 Quality, 1 Balanced, 0 Performance, 5 Ultra Performance)
  - RR: 0x10E41E02 latest on/off; 0x10E41DF7 preset (D/E/F)
  - FG: 0x10E41E03 latest on/off; 0x10E41DF1 preset; 0x10308298 mode (2 fixed, 4 dynamic); 0x104D6667 and 0x10562D0F factor 2x-6x
  - NR preset: 0x10E41DF8
- If NVAPI returns -137 (needs admin), it re-runs elevated with PowerShell Start-Process -Verb RunAs.
- DLSS indicator: HKLM\SOFTWARE\NVIDIA Corporation\Global\NGXCore. ShowDlssIndicator is a DWORD of 0 or 1024. DLSSG_IndicatorText is 0/1/2 for off/short/detailed. This needs admin.

6. Restore. The manifest replays backups from _DLSS5_Backup and deletes added files and dirs. lecram v11/v12 also creates a dlss5-nr-runtime\ copy (~500 MB), which restore removes.

supported_games:
There is no game allowlist. Support is decided by a detection rule in app/src/shared/install-routes.js (routesFor/recommendedRoute) using scan.js results: exe bitness (32/64), graphics API (dxgi DX11/DX12, d3d9, d3d8/ddraw, opengl, vulkan; DX10 is excluded), whether the game ships a native nvngx_dlss.dll that the tool did not add, and whether it is an emulator.
- Native DLSS + DX12 64-bit → 'native' (lecram RenoDX).
- No DLSS → Feeder, the default for DX9-12, Vulkan, OpenGL, 32-bit and emulators.
- 64-bit DX11/12/D3D9 → also ShortFuse 'renodx'.
- OptiScaler route → 64-bit dxgi/vulkan with native DLSS.
- Blocked: Mod Organizer Stock Game folders, loader conflicts and DX10.
- Anti-cheat detection is a warning, not a block. It matches easyanticheat, battleye, eac/be launcher or eaanticheat file names within depth 2, plus a hard-coded ARC Raiders path.
- GPU: NVIDIA's NR runtime only starts on RTX 50 (Blackwell, matched by regex RTX 50xx or RTX PRO Blackwell) with driver >= 616.56. Recommended driver is 616.64+; 617.42 is known good; 621.01 crashes lecram's add-on.
- RTX 20/30/40 needs the optional modified 310.8.SF-v2 DLL (model A only, slow).
- AMD/Intel: experimental vendor-neutral OptiScaler F5 port (DirectML, very slow: about 130 to 25 fps on a Radeon in Witcher 3).
- GPU detection uses nvidia-smi plus PCI vendor IDs from the registry. Override with the DLSS_AIO_FORCE_GPU env var.
- Only RenoDX HDR mods use a catalogue (the RenoDX snapshot release).
reuse_options:
MIT allows PlayOut (closed source) to reimplement or port any of the tool's own code as long as the MIT notice is kept in its third-party notices. This covers the route logic, the backup manifest, the nr-model INI writer and the NvDrs.cs DRS/indicator helper. No GPL helper is needed for this part. Options, best first:
1. Reimplement in PlayOut's main process (Node):
   - SR/RR/FG DLL update from NVIDIA/DLSS releases with a signature and version check.
   - The DRS writes. Port NvDrs.cs, or compile it as a small MIT helper exe; the NVAPI QueryInterface IDs and struct sizes are in that file.
   - The NGXCore indicator registry values.
   - NR preset INI keys: ReShade.ini [RenoDX.DLSS5] NRPreset, and OptiScaler.ini [DlssNr] Preset.
2. Treat the third-party payloads as runtime downloads (as AiO does), never bundled:
   - ReShade (BSD-3), DLSS5-Feeder (MIT) and GITC Uplift (MIT) are easy.
   - RenoDX add-ons are under RenoDX's license.
   - The OptiScaler DLSS-NR / F5 builds are GPL-3.0. Downloading the unmodified official release at runtime and only writing its INI does not make PlayOut a derivative. If PlayOut ever ships or modifies them, that goes in a separate public GPL helper, per PlayOut's policy.
3. The DLSS 5 runtime nvngx_dlssnr.dll is the legal weak point. It is NOT in NVIDIA's public SDK and is mirrored from games in RankFTW/rhi-repo, which has no license. PlayOut should not host it. Best is to download from the same mirror at runtime with the pinned SHA-256 + NVIDIA signature check, or let the user import their own, with a note. The modified 310.8.SF-v2 build is a modified NVIDIA binary; offer it only behind an explicit warning, or skip it.
4. Calling the upstream AiO app is not practical. It is a GUI Electron app with no CLI apart from nv-drs.exe, which has a clean CLI (get/set/indicator/sigcheck, JSON output) and could be rebuilt from MIT source.
Simplest MVP for the Upgrade menu: one "DLSS 5 (RTX 50)" action that runs the 'native' route (ReShade + lecram RenoDX add-on + nvngx_dlssnr.dll) for DX12 games with DLSS, and the Feeder route otherwise. Add a model A/B selector and Restore from a _PlayOut backup manifest.
anticheat_risk: High for multiplayer. DLSS 5 here always injects code: a ReShade proxy DLL (dxgi.dll/d3d9.dll/opengl32.dll or a global Vulkan layer), a ReShade add-on (.addon64), extra NGX/Streamline DLLs, or an OptiScaler proxy. The README says plainly "Single-player games only. Games with anti-cheat may treat injected files as cheating – risk of a ban." The tool only warns (shared/anti-cheat-warning.js, a main-process confirm dialog, consent per install, never stored). The warning is triggered by EasyAntiCheat, BattlEye, EA AntiCheat or launcher files, and a hard-coded ARC Raiders path. It does not cover Vanguard, Ricochet, FACEIT and similar. DRS-only changes (driver profile presets) and DLL version swaps carry a lower risk than injection, but signed-file checks in some anti-cheats can still flag swapped DLLs. PlayOut should combine its Steam-tag warning (Multiplayer, PvP, Competitive and so on) with the file-based anti-cheat detection.
pitfalls:
- The GPU gate matters most. NVIDIA's NR runtime only starts on RTX 50 (Blackwell) with driver >= 616.56; other cards fail with "NR runtime did not start". RTX 20-40 needs the modified, unsigned 310.8.SF-v2 DLL (model A, about half the fps). AMD/Intel needs the experimental DirectML OptiScaler F5 port (huge fps loss).
- Driver 621.01 crashes lecram's add-on at game start (Witcher 3 access violation). 617.42 is known good. The tool has a driverNeuralFault check for driver >= 616.64 with certain consumer builds.
- Model choice is per INI, not DRS. NRPreset is in ReShade.ini, which ReShade only creates on first launch, so it must be pre-created. The 0x10E41DF8 DRS NR preset exists but the 310.9.x runtime ignores it.
- Loader conflicts: an existing ASI ReShade, multiple ReShade hooks, other dxgi/d3d proxies, Mod Organizer Stock Game, and Vulkan wrappers like DXVK all have to be detected.
- An old D3DCompiler_47.dll beside the exe (e.g. Spider-Man Remastered) silently breaks the cs_5_1 NR shader.
- Never downgrade a newer DLSS DLL the game ships. Never overwrite the game's sl.* Streamline (ABI). Match bitness when replacing nested Unreal DLLs.
- The game must be closed (the exe is locked otherwise). The folder must be writable; Program Files and Xbox/WindowsApps folders are not.
- DRS writes and the HKLM NGXCore indicator may need admin (UAC). The tool creates its own driver profile, "DLSS5 Swapper - <exe>".
- Updates via Steam verify may revert DLLs, and the backup manifest must handle that.
- lecram v11/v12 creates a ~500 MB dlss5-nr-runtime folder.
- NR costs performance on top of SR (about 3-6 ms per frame).
- The ecosystem moves fast (10 releases in 4 weeks, pinned SHA-256 of third-party builds), so pins go stale quickly.
- Legal: the NR DLL mirror has no license.

exists_and_active: Exists and is very active. 8,158 stars, not archived, default branch main, last push 2026-11-08. Latest release v1.2.7.0 came out 2026-10-18. It is a WinUI 3 / C# (.NET) app, signed through SignPath, and also on winget (beeradmoore.dlss-swapper).
what_it_does: It scans installed games from Steam, GOG, Epic, Ubisoft Connect, Xbox App, Battle.net and manually added folders for known upscaler and frame-gen DLLs. It downloads chosen versions of those DLLs from its own CDN, then swaps them into the game folder: it keeps a one-time backup of the original, copies the new DLL over every instance of that file type, and can restore the original later. Supported types are DLSS (super resolution), DLSS-G (frame gen), DLSS-D (ray reconstruction), FSR 3.1 (DX12 and Vulkan), XeSS, XeSS DX11, XeSS-FG and XeLL. It cannot add DLSS to a game that has none. It also has extras: the NGX on-screen DLSS indicator and logging (registry), DLSS preset JSONs, user import of DLL zips, and a per-game swap history.
mechanism:
DISCOVERY (src/Data/Game.cs ProcessGame): Directory.GetFiles(InstallPath, "*.dll") recurses the whole install folder, using EnumerationOptions with RecurseSubdirectories=true and AttributesToSkip |= ReparsePoint (it does not follow junctions or symlinks). Each file NAME is matched exactly and case-sensitively (dllName == ...):
- nvngx_dlss.dll -> DLSS
- nvngx_dlssg.dll -> DLSS_G (frame generation)
- nvngx_dlssd.dll -> DLSS_D (ray reconstruction)
- amd_fidelityfx_dx12.dll -> FSR_31_DX12
- amd_fidelityfx_vk.dll -> FSR_31_VK
- libxess.dll -> XeSS
- libxess_dx11.dll -> XeSS_DX11
- libxess_fg.dll -> XeSS_FG
- libxell.dll -> XeLL (Intel low-latency)
The same table is in DLLManager.DllNameForGameAssetType. Only the FSR 3.1+ FidelityFX API loader DLL is swappable. Older FSR2-era names (ffx_fsr2_api_*.dll) and the ffx_* SDK2 or Streamline sl.*.dll / DirectStorage enum values in GameAssetType.cs are not swapped (the manifest lists directstorage arrays as empty). Version comes from FileVersionInfo (major.minor.build.private, packed as a ulong version_number = major<<48 | minor<<32 | build<<16 | private). The hash is the uppercase MD5 of the whole file. For amd_fidelityfx_*.dll it also calls LoadLibrary and the exported ffxQuery (FFX_API_QUERY_DESC_TYPE_GET_VERSIONS=4, createDescType UPSCALE=0x00010000) to list the FSR versions inside, which runs vendor code in-process (Helpers/FSR31/FSR31Helper.cs).

MANIFEST: remote https://beeradmoore.github.io/dlss-swapper/manifest.json (GitHub Pages; source is docs/manifest.json in the repo). A copy is cached in local storage, and a bundled src/Assets/static_manifest.json is the fallback. It is re-downloaded on an "Update manifest" action, and an identical file is ignored. Top-level shape: { "dlss":[], "dlss_d":[], "dlss_g":[], "fsr_31_dx12":[], "fsr_31_vk":[], "xess":[], "xell":[], "xess_fg":[], "xess_dx11":[], "directstorage":[], "directstorage_core":[], "known_dlls":{...} }. Each record (DLLRecord): version, version_number, internal_name, internal_name_extra, additional_label, md5_hash (of the DLL), zip_md5_hash (of the zip), download_url, file_description, signed_datetime, is_signature_valid, is_dev_file, file_size, zip_file_size, dll_source (for example "TechPowerUp"). As of today the counts and newest entries are:
- dlss: 114, newest 310.9.16.0
- dlss_d: 27, newest 310.9.16.0
- dlss_g: 41, newest 310.9.16.0
- fsr_31_dx12: 9, newest 1.0.2.38022
- fsr_31_vk: 7, newest 1.0.1.42386
- xess: 15, newest 2.0.2.68
- xell: 7, newest 1.3.2.10
- xess_fg: 9, newest 1.3.1.78
- xess_dx11: 3, newest 2.0.2.68
Records are sorted ascending, so to get the "latest" take the max version_number and skip is_dev_file=true. "known_dlls" maps each type to [{hash, version, sources:{LibraryName:[base64(game title)]}}]. It is crowd-sourced telemetry of which hashes ship in which games, used only to flag "unknown" DLLs. It is not an allowlist.

DOWNLOAD (DLLRecord.DownloadAsync): it fetches download_url, for example https://dlss-swapper-downloads.beeradmoore.com/dlss/dlss_v310.9.16.0_C77DDAE731F54720DDEEEE06AC356C5A.zip. That is beeradmoore's own Cloudflare-fronted host (HEAD returns 200, 45 MB, application/x-zip-compressed). The zip goes to a temp GUID.zip and its MD5 is checked against zip_md5_hash. If it matches, the single entry whose Name equals the expected DLL name (case-insensitive) is extracted into the app's DLL store at LocalRecord.ExpectedPath.

SWAP (Game.UpdateDllAsync):
1. Check that the downloaded DLL's MD5 equals md5_hash.
2. Unless Settings.AllowUntrusted is on, require WinTrust.VerifyEmbeddedSignature(path) to pass. This is WinVerifyTrust with WINTRUST_ACTION_GENERIC_VERIFY_V2 on the embedded Authenticode signature. It does NOT pin the signer to NVIDIA/AMD/Intel, so any validly signed file passes.
3. If no backup exists for this type, File.Copy each existing instance to "<path>.dlsss" next to the original (never overwriting an existing .dlsss).
4. File.Copy the new DLL over every instance of that type in the game (overwrite=true).
5. Write GameHistory rows (SQLite). On UnauthorizedAccessException it offers to relaunch as admin (Xbox/WindowsApps or Program Files).

RESTORE (Game.ResetDllAsync): File.Move("<path>.dlsss" -> "<path>", overwrite).

GAME UPDATE HANDLING: on rescan, if a DLL's version changed externally (a game update), the stale .dlsss backup is DELETED and history records "DLLChangedExternally". Settings.IgnoredPaths excludes folders. Other registry use: DLSSSettingsManager runs elevated "reg add" on the NGXCore key for ShowDlssIndicator, LogLevel and LoggingWindow (global DLSS overlay and logging). Nothing here uses NVAPI DRS for the swap itself.

supported_games: No game allowlist. A game is supported if a recursive *.dll scan of its install folder finds any of the exact file names above. The "known_dlls" list in the manifest only marks a found DLL hash as known or unknown, and unknown ones are reported for telemetry. There is NO anti-cheat or online-game denylist. The only safeguard is a one-time dialog on first launch (Settings.HasShownMultiplayerWarning, resource key MainWindow_NoteForMultiplayerGames_Message), which warns that anti-cheat may not tolerate changed files. Users can exclude folders with Settings.IgnoredPaths. Libraries scanned: Steam (libraryfolders.vdf + appmanifest .acf), GOG (Galaxy DB), Epic (LauncherInstalled.dat + manifests), Ubisoft Connect, Xbox App, Battle.net (product.db protobuf), and manual adds.
reuse_options:
PlayOut can and should reimplement this in its own closed-source TypeScript. The mechanism is simple: a fixed table of file names, recursive glob without following reparse points, FileVersionInfo version, MD5, a .dlsss sidecar backup, copy over, and restore by move. None of that is copyrightable expression, so no GPL helper is needed as long as no C# source is copied verbatim. Reading the manifest JSON at runtime is reuse of factual data, not code, and creates no GPL linkage. Still, credit DLSS Swapper and ideally tell beeradmoore. Do not bundle the C# code or the DLSS Swapper exe.

Options for the DLL binaries, in order of preference:
(a) Fetch beeradmoore's manifest and CDN zips at runtime, after getting the author's permission. This is the simplest option, but it has no formal terms and costs him bandwidth.
(b) Build PlayOut's own small manifest of only the latest version per type, with URLs pointing to vendor-hosted sources. NVIDIA's github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS releases and repo contain the current nvngx_dlss/dlssg/dlssd. Intel's github.com/intel/xess releases contain libxess*.dll. AMD's FidelityFX SDK (MIT) GitHub releases contain amd_fidelityfx_dx12/vk.dll.
(c) Never re-host NVIDIA DLLs on PlayOut's own Drive or CDN as a stand-alone download. The NVIDIA RTX SDK license forbids stand-alone distribution, and the legal status of DLSS Swapper's own CDN is grey.

For the "latest" pick: max version_number and is_dev_file=false. Verify the zip MD5, the DLL MD5 and the Authenticode signature. Ideally also pin the signer subject to "NVIDIA Corporation", "Advanced Micro Devices" or "Intel Corporation", which DLSS Swapper does not do. In Electron, run PowerShell Get-AuthenticodeSignature or a tiny native call. Do not use the LoadLibrary/ffxQuery trick for FSR version reading in the Electron main process; read the PE version resource instead.
anticheat_risk: Moderate. Replacing signed vendor DLLs is not a hook or injection, but it changes game files. Integrity checks or anti-cheat (EAC, BattlEye, Vanguard, Ricochet, FACEIT, VAC file checks) may refuse to launch, flag the file, or in the worst case act on the account. DLSS Swapper itself has no per-game detection and only shows a generic one-time warning (its issue #442 "is it safe to swap DLSS in online games?" and #80 multiplayer support matrix were never resolved into a list). Many anti-cheat titles also verify files, so Steam "verify integrity" or a game update reverts the swap. The user's planned Steam-tag warning (Free to Play / PvP / eSports / Competitive / Team-Based / MMO / Online Co-Op / Multiplayer) should fire before any swap. Swaps that keep official vendor-signed DLLs (signature still valid) are much lower risk than OptiScaler-style proxy DLLs (dxgi.dll/winmm.dll), which are true injection.
pitfalls:
- File-name matching is case-sensitive in DLSS Swapper (dllName == ...). PlayOut should match case-insensitively but write back to the exact existing path.
- A game can contain several copies of the same DLL (for example engine plus plugin folders). DLSS Swapper overwrites ALL of them and backs up each one, and so should PlayOut.
- Backups go next to the DLL as <name>.dlsss. Only one generation is kept, and an existing backup is never overwritten, so the backup stays the original game file.
- When a game update changes the DLL, the old backup is stale and should be deleted (DLSS Swapper does this on rescan). Steam verify or updates silently revert swaps, so rescan the version when the page opens.
- Xbox/Game Pass (WindowsApps) and Program Files installs need admin, and WindowsApps is often not writable at all. Handle EPERM and offer elevation or skip.
- Skip reparse points and junctions while recursing, to avoid loops and other drives.
- The recursive *.dll scan of big games is slow, so run it in a worker and cache the results.
- FSR: only the FSR 3.1+ loader (amd_fidelityfx_dx12.dll / amd_fidelityfx_vk.dll) is swappable. FSR 2 / 3.0 are statically linked or use ffx_fsr2_api_x64.dll and cannot be upgraded this way. FSR4 on RDNA4 comes via the AMD driver override on top of a 3.1 DLL.
- DLSS 4/4.5 files are version 310.x (latest in the manifest is 310.9.16.0). Newer DLSS needs the right preset or driver override (NVIDIA app / NVAPI DRS) to actually use the transformer model, so a DLL swap alone may not change the model.
- DLSS-G (frame gen) swaps can break games whose Streamline sl.*.dll is too old. Swapping nvngx_dlssg.dll without matching Streamline can crash. Mixing upscaler and frame-gen versions is a common crash source, so keep restore one click away.
- WinVerifyTrust in DLSS Swapper does not check WHO signed the file.
- The CDN zips are large (DLSS 310 is about 45 MB). Show progress and verify MD5.
- The known_dlls game titles are base64 encoded.
- No written terms exist for the manifest or CDN, and the CDN is the author's personal infrastructure.
- The DLSS Swapper source is GPL-3.0, so do not paste its C# into the closed-source app.

The repo does match the description, and its real scope is bigger than "cache shaders": it builds and pre-warms the GPU driver's own pipeline cache.
what_it_does:
It pre-compiles a game's real D3D12/D3D11 (and Vulkan) pipelines into the GPU driver's own on-disk shader cache before you play, with the game closed. The game then finds them in the driver cache instead of compiling mid-frame, which removes shader compilation stutter. Things it does NOT do: download prebuilt driver caches, change shader cache size by default, use Steam shader pre-caching, or edit drivers. The README FAQ says it does not touch drivers or their settings and compiles through DirectX the way the game would. Its main features:
- Finds games in Steam, Epic, EA app, GOG, Ubisoft, Xbox PC, Battle.net, HoYoPlay, Gaijin, Riot and others, plus games added by hand.
- Reads the shaders a game ships with through engine-specific readers.
- Plans which pipelines (PSOs) the game will build.
- Compiles them in a staged process named like the game's exe, so the driver files them under that game's cache key.
- Re-compiles after driver updates, which wipe the cache, through a scheduled task.
- An optional "recorder" (a proxy d3d12.dll/d3d11.dll dropped into the game folder) records pipelines while you play, for games whose files alone are not enough.
- An optional Patreon-gated community shader-hash database.
- Frame-time graphs and before/after measurements.
Results it publishes, all on an RTX 5090: FF7 Rebirth went from 19 stutters to 0, Jedi Survivor from 9,038 to 11, and Hogwarts from 1,014 to 87. It fixes shader stutter only, not traversal or streaming stutter.
mechanism:
From source and ARCHITECTURE.md. The pipeline (Core, src/SCSKiller.Core) runs 8 steps:

1. Scan (Games/*Source.cs). Each store has a reader. SteamSource parses libraryfolders/appmanifest, and there are Epic, EA, GOG, Xbox, Battle.net and other sources. GameFiles.GameExe picks the real exe (for Unreal, the -Shipping.exe). GameFiles is also the anti-cheat detector, and Vac.cs handles VAC. Verdicts are cached in scan.json.
2. Read. An engine reader per engine lists the shipped shaders as a ShaderIndex. There are readers for Unreal, Unity, FromSoft, RE Engine, RED Engine, Northlight, Dagor, RAGE, Source2, Naughty Dog, Santa Monica, Nixxes, Decima, Luminous, ForzaTech, BlackSpace, Snowdrop, Frostbite, CryEngine, and "Carved" (raw DXBC/DXIL). Archive AES keys come from the game exe, the user or a pinned download.
3. Check. Planner.Check returns Unsupported, NeedsRecording or Ready. Ready without a recording needs a state-independent cache (NVIDIA) plus a root-signature rule for the engine version, from plan-rules.json and confirmed-engines.json.
4. Prepare. The local recording.db is merged with the community download, and shader bytes are re-read from the install by hash.
5. Plan. plan.bin is written.
6. Materialize. The shader bytes are copied into a work\ folder.
7. Warm. scskiller_warm.exe (proxy/warm.cpp, warm11.cpp) stages a copy of itself renamed to the game's exe name, plus the recorder DLL and the databases, in a temp folder. It runs it, the DLL in warm mode creates every pipeline on a real D3D12/D3D11 device, and the driver writes its cache. For Vulkan it replays .foz files with a patched Fossilize. work\ is then deleted, and a scskiller.warmed marker plus compiled.keys are written.
8. Track. A driver or game update marks the game Stale. The scheduled task runs `scskillerw.exe rewarm-stale --if-driver-changed` to compile again.

Driver cache facts:
- NVIDIA D3D12 cache is keyed by exe file name (packaged/Xbox games by package identity). Files are %LOCALAPPDATA%\NVIDIA\DXCache\*.nvph, and Vulkan uses NVIDIA\GLCache.
- AMD uses AMD\DxcCache / VkCache. For Vulkan it uses AMD_VK_PIPELINE_CACHE_PATH and _FILENAME. Under Steam's redirect it uses AMDv1\steamapp_shader_cache.parc.
- %LOCALAPPDATA%\D3DSCache is the Windows runtime cache.

Driver settings it can change, only when asked:
- `cache set <GB|unlimited|default>` writes the NVIDIA DRS setting "Shader disk cache maximum size" through NvAPI_DRS (id 0x00AC8497 on 610.88, looked up by name). It runs elevated.
- `nvidia-auto-shader off|low|medium|high` switches NVIDIA's own Auto Shader Compilation and needs admin.
- `cache clear <game> [--game-precache]` deletes driver caches, D3DSCache, and the game's own caches such as *.ushaderprecache.

The recorder (proxy/proxy.cpp built as d3d12.dll, optional):
- It is installed into the game folder with scskiller.cfg, and only into games with no anti-cheat, no VAC, writable and not running.
- It chains to an existing mod d3d12.dll by renaming it d3d12.scskiller-next.dll. On AMD AGS games it goes in as amd_ags_x64.dll. With Streamline it uses a preloader DLL.
- The scskiller.db inbox is imported into %LOCALAPPDATA%\SCSKiller\...\recording.db.
- Turning it off removes exactly the files it added.

Backup and restore: compiling never modifies game files, and the README says "Game files are never modified". Only the recorder adds files, and they are removed on disable or uninstall.

Data locations:
- App state: %LOCALAPPDATA%\SCSKiller\ (or data\ next to the portable exe).
- Compiled output: the driver's own cache.

CLI (src/SCSKiller.Cli, shipped as cli\scskiller.exe and the windowless cli\scskillerw.exe in the release zip) offers:
- scan [--rescan]
- status [game]
- compile <game|--all-ready> [--threads N] [--idle|--when-idle] [--careful|--fast] [--rt-only]
- queue
- rewarm-stale
- cache get/set/page/clear
- nvidia-snapshot
- nvidia-auto-shader
- record install|uninstall|remove-all|clear|alongside <game>
- shared <game> on|off|follow
- key <game> <hex>
- add <exe>
- exe <game> <exe>|auto

Output is human-readable text. Only the elevated cache set / nvidia-auto-shader calls have `--result <file>`, which writes JSON. Game ids look like steam:<appid>, epic:<appname>, xbox:<PFN>, ea:<id>.

supported_games:
There is no fixed allowlist. Support is decided per game at run time.
- Engine detection: a game needs an engine reader that can read its shipped shaders. There are roughly 22 engine families plus "Carved", which handles any raw DXBC/DXIL.
- The Planner check then gives each game one of three results:
  - Ready: on NVIDIA when its engine version has a root-signature rule.
  - NeedsRecording: play a few minutes with the recorder on, or use the community database.
  - Unsupported.
- known-stutter.json (embedded, and served at dl.scskiller.io/v1/content/known-stutter.json) is only a "recommended / known to stutter" ranking of about 40 entries with sources. It is not a gate.
- Some games prepare their own shaders at boot (precompiles-at-boot.json) and are flagged.
- APIs: DirectX 12 on NVIDIA and AMD. DirectX 11 on NVIDIA only (AMD D3D11 is partial, input layouts via recorder). Vulkan on NVIDIA and AMD (it needs a recorded .foz).
- GPUs: NVIDIA and AMD. Intel is experimental behind Settings.ExperimentalIntel ("not supported yet" per the README).
- OS: Windows 10 2004+ or 11 x64. A Linux AppImage also exists.
- Anti-cheat games: the shader files are read and the compile still runs, because compiling happens outside the game. But they never get the recorder unless the user opts in per session.
reuse_options:
Recommended: call the upstream CLI as a separate program, PlayOut's normal pattern.
- Download the official SCSKiller-<ver>-Portable.zip from GitHub Releases at the user's request and check it against SHA256SUMS-unsigned.txt.
- Extract it next to PlayOut, for example in an Upgrades\SCSKiller folder. The CLI looks for native\ at ..\native\, so keep the zip's folder layout.
- Run cli\scskiller.exe from Electron with child_process. Useful calls:
  - `scan`
  - `status <game>`
  - `compile <steam:appid> --idle`
  - `cache clear <game>`
  - `record install|uninstall <game>` (avoid this)
- Parse the stdout text. There is no general JSON mode, so the parser will be brittle across versions; pin a version or match patterns defensively.
- Calling a GPL program over its command line is arm's-length use, not linking, so PlayOut can stay closed source. PlayOut must still keep the license and notices and point users to the source if it redistributes the binaries. Downloading at run time from upstream avoids redistribution entirely.
- The CLI and the GUI share %LOCALAPPDATA%\SCSKiller state, so a user who also has the app installed sees the same queue and plans.

Reimplementing it inside closed PlayOut is not realistic and not allowed. The value is in about 1.1 MB of ScsKiller.cs, the engine readers, the planner, and the C++ warm/proxy (proxy.cpp alone is about 440 KB). Copying any of it would be a GPL derived work.

The embedded JSON data files (known-stutter.json and others) are GPL-licensed repo content. Copying them into closed PlayOut is legally murky; fetching them at run time, or keeping them in a public GPL helper, is safer.

If PlayOut needs a tighter integration (JSON output, a progress stream), build a small public GPL helper in its own repo, as with the Co-Op and PS5PKG helpers. It could be a thin fork or wrapper of SCSKiller.Cli that adds `--json` output, published separately. Fork etiquette applies: own name, say it is unofficial, keep the notices.

The simplest option of all: offer to install SCSKiller and open it, or launch it, with PlayOut showing a "Compile shaders" entry that calls the CLI.
anticheat_risk:
Low for the compile path. Compiling only reads game files and runs scskiller_warm.exe, a renamed copy staged in SCSKiller's own temp folder, outside the game process. The game folder and the game process are untouched, and the result sits in the driver's normal cache, so no ban risk is known from compile-only use.

Higher for the recorder:
- It puts a proxy d3d12.dll/d3d11.dll (or amd_ags_x64.dll, or a preloader DLL) plus scskiller.cfg into the game folder and hooks the D3D12 device in-process.
- SCSKiller refuses it in games with detected anti-cheat or VAC, and re-checks every 2 minutes.
- Exceptions need explicit opt-in:
  - The ELDEN RING / ARMORED CORE VI offline-without-EAC session adds d3d12.dll + scskiller.cfg + steam_appid.txt.
  - The setting "Allow the recorder in games with anti-cheat (at your own risk)".
- The README warns that if these files are left behind and the game is started online, "you could be banned", and that its anti-cheat check can miss a game.

For PlayOut:
- Never run `record install` on games tagged Multiplayer, PvP, Competitive, Online Co-Op and similar.
- Still show the user's requested anti-cheat warning when Shader Cache is enabled on such tagged games.
- Treat compile-only as low risk; recording is the risky part.
pitfalls:
- Very young and fast-moving: 7 weeks old, about 40 releases. CLI text output and flags can change, so pin a version or parse defensively.
- Releases are unsigned. SmartScreen warns and Windows 11 Smart App Control blocks the binaries outright.
- Large download: about 117 MB portable zip, self-contained .NET 10 plus the Windows App SDK.
- GPU and API limits:
  - NVIDIA/AMD only; Intel is experimental and hidden.
  - D3D11 is NVIDIA-only.
  - Vulkan needs a recording.
  - Many games come back NeedsRecording, which means the user plays with the recorder injected or holds a Patreon-gated community database.
  - "Ready without recording" mainly applies on NVIDIA for engines with confirmed root-signature rules.
- Results are driver-specific. Every GPU driver update clears the cache, so a re-compile is needed. Upstream uses a scheduled task (rewarm-stale --if-driver-changed); PlayOut would need its own trigger or have to register theirs.
- The NVIDIA cache key is the exe file name. Two games with the same exe name share a key, and the compile must stage the right exe name.
- Compiling is heavy: many threads and long run times. The game must be closed while it compiles.
- cache set and nvidia-auto-shader need elevation (UAC) and change global NVIDIA DRS settings. Avoid them or ask first.
- The CLI and the app share %LOCALAPPDATA%\SCSKiller state and named mutexes, so running both at once can conflict over locks and queue.
- The community database and update feeds go through dl.scskiller.io, SCSKiller's server, with Patreon auth and no public API terms. Don't call them directly from PlayOut.
- The CLI refuses to run on dev builds (AppStore.RefusesLiveData). Official builds only.
- It fixes shader stutter only, not traversal stutter. Some games show "engine prepares its own shaders" and gain little.

what_it_does: OptiScaler is a middleware DLL proxy. It intercepts the upscaler calls a game already makes (DLSS2+, FSR2+ or XeSS "inputs") and sends them to the backend the user picks in its overlay ("outputs"): XeSS, FSR 2/3/4 or DLSS. It can also swap or add frame generation: OptiFG on DX12, XeFG, FSR3/4-FG, or Nukem's DLSSG-to-FSR3. On AMD/Intel GPUs it spoofs an NVIDIA GPU over DXGI (Dxgi=auto, which means true on non-NVIDIA) so the game shows its DLSS options, and those DLSS inputs are then served by FSR or XeSS. fakenvapi supplies a fake nvapi that exposes Reflex and DLSS-FG and turns Reflex into AMD Anti-Lag 2, LatencyFlex or XeLL. The in-game overlay opens with Insert. Supported APIs: DX11, DX12, Vulkan. OptiClick is a closed-source one-click installer for less experienced users. It scans Steam (or a folder you pick), downloads the latest OptiScaler, and applies per-game and per-GPU settings from its own database: upscaler choice, XeFG frame generation, FSR4 INT8, RTSS tweaks, and Engine.ini edits. It also chooses a DLL proxy name that avoids clashes with ReShade and similar mods, and installs extras when a game needs them: OptiPatcher, REFramework, and the alxn1 d3d12-proxy UE5 GI fix. It is restricted to its own supported-games list (about 160 games in the wiki's newly-supported list block) and to these GPUs: Intel Arc; AMD RX 6000/7000/9000 and 780M/880M/890M/8050S/8060S; NVIDIA RTX 20-50.
mechanism:
OptiClick is closed source, so the reference install procedure below comes from OptiScaler's official setup_windows.bat (master "v3.0-pre1" and release/0.9 "v2.8") and from the wiki pages Automated-Installation, Manual-Installation, Uninstallation, Updating-Optiscaler and Compatibility-with-other-mods.

1) DOWNLOAD. GitHub API repos/optiscaler/OptiScaler/releases/latest returns one .7z asset per release. The name follows "Optiscaler_<ver>-final.<yyyymmdd>[._suffix].7z"; suffixes have included "._MM" and "._Reup", so match by .7z extension and not by an exact name. It is a 7-Zip archive, so PlayOut needs a 7z extractor (7za or 7zip-bin).

2) ARCHIVE LAYOUT for 0.9.x stable, built from release/0.9 vcxproj PostBuildEvent plus the bundles listed in the 0.9.5 notes. Everything sits flat in one folder: OptiScaler.dll, OptiScaler.ini, libxess.dll, libxess_dx11.dll and other XeSS SDK DLLs, amd_fidelityfx_vk.dll, amd_fidelityfx_dx12.dll (the renamed FFX v2 loader), amd_fidelityfx_upscaler_dx12.dll, amd_fidelityfx_framegeneration_dx12.dll, D3D12_Optiscaler\ (Agility SDK D3D12Core.dll etc.), Licenses\, setup_windows.bat, setup_linux.sh and a "!! EXTRACT ALL FILES TO GAME FOLDER !!" marker file. The packed 0.9.5 build also bundles fakenvapi 1.4.1 (fakenvapi.dll, fakenvapi.ini), Nukem dlssg_to_fsr3_amd_is_better.dll 0.130, FFX 2.4 SDK (FSR 4.1.2) and XeSS 3.0.2. The master/v10 layout differs: the XeSS, FFX and Agility DLLs move into an OptiScaler\ subfolder (OptiScaler\D3D12_OptiScaler\, OptiScaler\plugins\), and only OptiScaler.dll, OptiScaler.ini and setup files stay at the root.

3) TARGET FOLDER. Extract ALL files next to the main game exe. For Unreal Engine games, use <Game>\<ProjectName>\Binaries\Win64 (or WinGDK), which is where *-Win64-Shipping.exe or *-WinGDK-Shipping.exe lives, and never the Engine folder. The bat warns if an .\Engine folder exists in the current directory. Wiki examples: Expedition 33\Sandfall\Binaries\Win64, Cyberpunk 2077\bin\x64, HITMAN 3\Retail, The Witcher 3\bin\x64_dx12, Warhammer 40,000 DARKTIDE\binaries.

4) RENAME. OptiScaler.dll is renamed to one of: dxgi.dll (default, most compatible), winmm.dll (recommended for Vulkan and also for Xbox/MS Store), version.dll (Xbox/MS Store; Infinity Nikki needs it), dbghelp.dll, d3d12.dll (try this if DLSS crashes on FSR-only games), wininet.dll, winhttp.dll, or OptiScaler.asi (only with Ultimate ASI Loader). If the chosen name already exists, the bat asks before overwriting. That file may be ReShade or another mod. Alternatives: pick another name, or move the other mod's DLL into a plugins\ folder (OptiScaler loads a same-named DLL from there). ReShade can also be renamed to ReShade64.dll with LoadReshade=true; for SpecialK use LoadSpecialK. OptiScaler.ini must keep its exact name.

5) INI EDITS. The bat does plain text replacements in OptiScaler.ini. (a) If the user is on AMD/Intel and says NO to DLSS inputs: "Dxgi=auto" becomes "Dxgi=false", which turns off NVIDIA spoofing. Under [Spoofing], Dxgi=auto means true on AMD/Intel and false on NVIDIA. There are also SpoofedVendorId, SpoofedDeviceId (default 4090), StreamlineSpoofing and Vulkan=auto. (b) If OptiPatcher is installed: "LoadAsiPlugins=auto" becomes "LoadAsiPlugins=true". NVIDIA is detected by %windir%\system32\nvapi64.dll; when present, spoofing questions are skipped. Other useful keys: Dx11Upscaler, Dx12Upscaler and VulkanUpscaler under [Upscalers]; FGInput and FGOutput under [FrameGen] (older docs used FGType=nukems); ShortcutKey; Fsr4ForceEnableInt8; LogLevel and LogToFile. OptiClick additionally writes per-game OptiScaler.ini and Unreal Engine.ini edits, changes RTSS settings for XeFG, and applies FSR4 INT8. Its exact values are in its private database.

6) OPTIPATCHER (AMD/Intel only). It unlocks DLSS and DLSSG inputs without spoofing. anticheat_risk: High for online and anti-cheat games. The OptiScaler README and the wiki Installation page both carry a caution: do not use this mod with online games, because it may trigger anti-cheat software and cause bans. OptiScaler works by dropping a proxy system DLL (dxgi, winmm, version, etc.) into the game folder, hooking DXGI, D3D and Vulkan, spoofing the GPU vendor as NVIDIA, and loading ASI plugins. Anti-cheat detects exactly these things. Compatibility list examples: EA Sports WRC fails because EA Anti-Cheat blocks unknown DLLs; Gears of War: Reloaded fails because of EAC; 7 Days to Die requires disabling EAC; Conan Exiles requires disabling BattlEye; Escape from Tarkov works only in SPT (no EAC); Infinity Nikki needs the signed build or its anti-cheat blocks it; Arknights: Endfield and GOALS are marked as online games to use at your own risk. OptiClick's LICENSE makes the same disclaimer (warnings, disabled online features, suspensions, permanent bans). It still lists online titles such as FINAL FANTASY XIV Online and Ready or Not, so being on its list does not mean a game is safe. PlayOut should show the Steam-tag multiplayer/PvP warning the user asked for, and should also warn when the install folder contains EasyAntiCheat\, BattlEye\, EAAntiCheat or similar, or when the compatibility-list notes mention anti-cheat.
pitfalls:
- Wrong folder. For Unreal Engine games the DLL must go in <Project>\Binaries\Win64 or WinGDK next to *-Shipping.exe, never the root launcher or Engine\; for other games, next to the real render exe, not the launcher (e.g. Witcher 3 bin\x64_dx12). Installing in the wrong place fails silently.
- DLL name clashes. dxgi.dll may already be ReShade, SpecialK or another mod (the wiki recommends winmm for Vulkan and winmm/version for Xbox/MS Store). Detect an existing file and offer another name or the plugins\ sideload, and never overwrite without a backup.
- 0.9.x overwrites game files. Its archive is flat and contains libxess.dll and amd_fidelityfx_dx12.dll, which can overwrite the game's own DLLs. The official uninstaller keeps them, so restoring is manual. Back up before extracting, and restore from the manifest on uninstall.
- Archive layout changes. The layout differs between 0.9 (flat) and v10 (OptiScaler\ subfolder, OptiScaler\plugins), and asset names vary ("._MM", "._Reup"). Derive the file list from the extracted archive instead of hardcoding it.
- Uninstall detection. Detect existing installs through the PE OriginalFilename == "OptiScaler.dll" check, and clean pre-0.9 leftovers (nvngx.dll, nvapi64.dll, OptiScaler.asi).
- Steam verify/update. Steam "verify integrity" or a game update can restore or overwrite the DLLs. Store a per-game manifest and re-check state when the game page opens.
- Write access. Game folders under Program Files or XboxGames (WindowsApps) may need admin, and MS Store/Xbox installs are often read-only.
- NVIDIA users. Spoofing is pointless, so skip the Dxgi question. Since 0.9.5, FSR4 needs AMD driver 26.10.1+ for HW flip metering, and XeFG needs borderless or fullscreen-windowed, has no Vulkan support and supports HDR10 only.
- RTSS and FSR-only games. RTSS needs "Use MS Detours API hooking" and, for XeFG, "Inject Reflex Markers" turned off. FSR2/3-only games need a user-supplied nvngx_dlss.dll for DLSS output; PlayOut must not redistribute NVIDIA's DLL.
- OptiPatcher versions. Its patches target the latest game version only.
- Plain text INI edits. The bat's edits assume default values ("Dxgi=auto"); do key-aware INI edits instead.
- Impersonation. The OptiScaler team warns about fake sites and unofficial manager apps, and says it does not support third-party installers. PlayOut must download only from github.com/optiscaler and must say it is not official.
- OptiClick integration. It can't be integrated (closed source, no CLI, private data).
- 7-Zip dependency. Extraction needs a 7z extractor.
hardware_requirements: OptiScaler runs on any DX11, DX12 or Vulkan-capable GPU; the outputs available depend on the vendor. XeSS works on all GPUs, while XeSS on native DX11 is Intel Arc only. FSR2/3 work everywhere. FSR4 is official on RDNA4 and RDNA3 dGPUs; with 0.9.5 (FSR 4.1.2) INT8 support extends officially to RDNA2 and Ryzen APUs, and other GPUs can force it with Fsr4ForceEnableInt8. DLSS output needs an NVIDIA RTX GPU. XeMFG is Intel Arc only. OptiFG is DX12 only. HW flip metering needs AMD driver 26.10.1+. OptiClick needs Windows 11, an internet connection, and Intel Arc, AMD RX 6000/7000/9000 or 780M/880M/890M/8050S/8060S, or NVIDIA RTX 20-50.

what_it_does:
It is a GUI over Windows 10+ WOF (Windows Overlay Filter) transparent file compression, the same thing `compact.exe /exe` does. The user picks a folder, and Steam games are auto-detected from their appmanifest .acf. The user then picks XPRESS4K, XPRESS8K, XPRESS16K or LZX, and the folder is compressed in place. Files stay readable by every program because the WOF driver decompresses them on the fly. Other features:
- Analysis of the folder's current state.
- Estimated savings, from a community database for Steam games or from an LZ4 sampling estimator for other folders.
- Skip lists for file types that compress poorly.
- Uncompress.
- A background Watcher that recompresses folders after Steam updates "decay" them.
- Optional anonymous submission of results to the community database.
mechanism:
COMPRESS (CompactGUI.Core/Compactor.cs). It does not call compact.exe.
- For each file it calls `File.OpenHandle(path)`, then `WofSetFileDataLocation(handle, WOF_PROVIDER_FILE=2, &WOF_FILE_COMPRESSION_INFO_V1{Algorithm, Flags=0}, 8)`.
- The Algorithm values are XPRESS4K=0, LZX=1, XPRESS8K=2, XPRESS16K=3. Note that LZX is 1 in the WOF enum, but CompactGUI's UI/database CompressionMode enum orders them X4K=0, X8K=1, X16K=2, LZX=3.
- HRESULT 0x80070158 (ERROR_COMPRESSION_NOT_BENEFICIAL) counts as success; the file simply stays uncompressed.
- Disk-full results trigger a retry mode that repeats while progress is made (RepeatWhileProgress).
- Work is spread across files in parallel. The worker count defaults to the number of CPUs (setting maxCompressionThreads, 0 = auto), and hard drives are locked to 1 thread by default (lockHDDsToOneThread).
- It drops to a single worker when free space is less than 2 x (half the total allocated size + the largest file), or when the folder holds a disk image (.vhd, .vhdx, .vmdk, .qcow2, .img).
- Files are left out of the working list when they are:
  - already in the chosen algorithm;
  - no larger than one cluster (GetDiskFreeSpace);
  - sparse;
  - reparse points (skipped during enumeration);
  - matched by the skip list (SkipListMatcher). The matcher uses Microsoft.Extensions.FileSystemGlobbing. A ".ext" or "*.ext" pattern matches `**/*.ext`, a bare name matches `**/name`, and absolute paths are made relative to the folder.

ANALYSE (Analyser.cs).
- It enumerates files recursively with IgnoreInaccessible and skips reparse points.
- Size on disk comes from `GetCompressedFileSize`.
- When size on disk differs from the file length, `WofIsExternalFile(path, &isExternal, &provider, &info, &len)` finds the algorithm. The FILE_ATTRIBUTE_COMPRESSED attribute means legacy LZNT1.
- It flags DirectStorage when any file is named dstorage.dll.
- Poorly compressed extensions are grouped by extension where compressed/uncompressed > 0.95.

UNCOMPRESS (Uncompactor.cs).
- It opens each file and calls `DeviceIoControl(handle, FSCTL_DELETE_EXTERNAL_BACKING = 0x90314, null, 0, null, 0, ...)`, in parallel.
- When disk space runs low it retries in order of file length.
- The compact.exe equivalent is `compact /u /s /a /i /exe "<dir>/*"`.

ESTIMATE.
- Steam games use the community database (WikiService.ParseData):
  - The overall ratio is the average of AfterBytes/BeforeBytes across the CompressionResults entries, weighted by TotalResults.
  - Per algorithm, the database's CompressionPercent (After/Before) is applied to the local folder's uncompressed size (SteamFolder.GetWikiResults).
  - Poorly compressed extensions from the database are used as a skip list only when their count is > 100 (`k.Value > 100`).
- Folders that are not Steam games use Estimator.cs, which is opt-in (EstimateCompressionForNonSteamFolders):
  - Each file is LZ4-compressed (K4os LZ4, L00_FAST) on a sample of up to 100 8 KB blocks spread across it, or the whole file if it is small.
  - On a hard drive it takes one contiguous chunk of 100 clusters from the middle of the file, with files sorted by first LCN (FSCTL_GET_RETRIEVAL_POINTERS).
  - Files with ratio >= 0.98 are added to the skip list.
  - Estimated after-bytes = sum(size x ratio), scaled by these fudge factors: X4K x1.01, X8K x1.0, X16K x0.98, LZX x0.95.

DEFAULT SKIP LIST (Settings.cs NonCompressableList): .dl_ .gif .jpg .jpeg .png .wmf .mkv .mp4 .wmv .avi .bik .bk2 .flv .ogg .mpg .m2v .m4v .vob .mp3 .aac .wma .flac .zip .xap .rar .7z .cab .lzx .docx .xlsx .pptx .vssx .vstx .onepkg .tar .gz .dmg .bz2 .tgz .lz .xz .txz.
- Per-folder options are SkipPoorlyCompressedFileTypes (global list), SkipUserSubmittedFiletypes (database extensions), a custom SkipList and a SkipListEnabled master toggle.

STEAM UPDATES / WATCHER (CompactGUI.Watcher).
- When Steam updates a game, the rewritten files are written uncompressed; WOF compression does not stick to new writes.
- The Watcher stores LastUncompressedSize, LastCompressedSize and LastCheckedSize for each watched folder.
- DecayPercentage = clamp((LastCheckedSize - LastCompressedSize) / (LastUncompressedSize - LastCompressedSize), 0, 1).
- An IdleDetector or a schedule (Never / IdleOnly / Scheduled / ScheduledAndIdle) runs BackgroundCompactor on folders with decay > 0 that are not recently modified and still have a compression level. It re-runs the same Compactor; already-compressed files are skipped because they are in the target algorithm.
- FolderChangeMonitor invalidates the cached analysis.

DATABASE SUBMISSION (optional). It sends an HTTP GET to a Google Form, entry.1019946248, with a JSON payload {UID, SteamID, GameName, FolderName, CompressionMode, BeforeBytes, AfterBytes, PoorlyCompressedExt}.

reuse_options:
1. Call compact.exe. This is the simplest option and there is no license issue, since compact.exe is part of Windows. PlayOut can spawn it from Electron.
- Compress: `compact.exe /c /s /a /i /exe:<xpress4k|xpress8k|xpress16k|lzx> "<gameDir>/*"`. /s recurses, /a includes hidden/system files and /i continues past errors.
- Uncompress: `compact.exe /u /s /a /i /exe "<gameDir>/*"`. The /exe flag is needed to remove WOF compression.
- Status: `compact /s /a /q`. The output is localized text, so parsing progress is fragile.
- compact.exe has no per-file skip list. To skip extensions PlayOut must pass file lists or call it per file or per directory, and that per-file spawning is slow.

2. Reimplement the mechanism in a small native helper, which is what CompactGUI does. Facts are not copyrightable, and Win32 APIs are public Microsoft APIs documented on MSDN. PlayOut can write its own clean code with:
- WofSetFileDataLocation (wofutil.dll) to compress;
- FSCTL_DELETE_EXTERNAL_BACKING to uncompress;
- WofIsExternalFile and GetCompressedFileSize to analyse.
Possible implementations are a small C# or Rust exe, a koffi/ffi-napi call from Node, or a PowerShell P/Invoke. This needs no GPL helper because no CompactGUI source is copied. This route gives per-file skip control, progress, cancellation and parallelism.

3. Reuse the database. database.json is fetched at runtime from GitHub raw and not bundled, so PlayOut uses it as a remote data source and does not ship it. That avoids GPL distribution obligations for the data, although the GPL's reach to factual data is unclear anyway. PlayOut should credit CompactGUI and its community database in the UI.

4. Call the upstream CompactGUI binary. Not recommended: it is a WPF GUI with no stable CLI.

5. Copy CompactGUI source (for example Estimator.cs or SkipListMatcher.cs). That would require a separate public GPL-3.0 helper, in line with PlayOut's existing pattern. It is unnecessary because the logic is simple to write independently.

Recommendation: write a clean-room implementation using the WOF APIs or compact.exe. Fetch database.json at runtime and use its CompressionResults for the savings estimate per algorithm and PoorlyCompressedExtensions (count > 100) as a skip list. Add PlayOut's own default skip list of extensions.
anticheat_risk: None in practice. WOF compression is a transparent filesystem feature. Game files keep identical contents when read, so hashes and integrity checks match, and no process or DLL is injected. Anti-cheat (EAC, BattlEye, Vanguard) and Steam "verify files" read the same bytes. Verify may report nothing, or Steam may rewrite files, which leaves them uncompressed. There are no known bans. It can still be listed in the Upgrade menu, but the multiplayer-tag ban warning does not really apply to compression; the load-time warning does.
pitfalls:
- **NTFS only.** Check the volume filesystem first.
- **Load times and CPU.** The user wants a warning that compression increases load times; that is the honest framing for fast NVMe drives. Decompression uses CPU on every read. The README says the impact is negligible and can even help on HDDs.
  - XPRESS4K is fastest to decompress and weakest. LZX compresses best but is slowest to compress and decompress.
  - Compression is CPU- and disk-heavy for a long time, so offer cancel and progress.
- **DirectStorage games.** Do not compress them; GPU decompression gains are lost. Detect dstorage.dll in the game folder and warn or block.
- **Writes undo compression.** Game updates, patches, mods (DLSS swap, OptiScaler) and Steam verify rewrite files uncompressed. Space "decays". Offer a recompress action, or track decay as Watcher does: store the sizes after compression and compare them later.
- **Disk space.** Compressing needs temporary free space per file, and very large files can fail with disk-full. Run one file at a time when space is low. Uncompressing needs free space for the full uncompressed size; check before running.
- **Running games.** Do not compress or uncompress while the game is running or Steam is updating it; locked files fail. Block when the game process is running.
- **Permissions.** WofSetFileDataLocation needs a handle that can write to the file. Steam libraries are usually user-writable, but Program Files and WindowsApps installs may need elevation or are impossible. Xbox/Game Pass encrypted folders cannot be done at all.
- **compact.exe quirks.** Its output is localized. /exe must be repeated on /u. Without /i it stops at the first error. It cannot skip by extension.
- **Mismatched enums.** WOF algorithm numbers (X4K=0, LZX=1, X8K=2, X16K=3) differ from the database CompType order (0=X4K, 1=X8K, 2=X16K, 3=LZX).
- **Database caveats.** Coverage is Steam appids only, and Confidence can be low with TotalResults=1. Show the estimate as approximate. Cache the roughly 9.5 MB file and refresh it no more than every 6 hours, as CompactGUI does.
- **Already-compressed files.** Skip sparse files, files no larger than one cluster, reparse points and disk images. Treat ERROR_COMPRESSION_NOT_BENEFICIAL (0x80070158) as OK.
- **Legacy compression.** Files with the FILE_ATTRIBUTE_COMPRESSED attribute use legacy LZNT1, a different mechanism; detect it separately.
